porbos.title: When Words Failed • That Noon in the Courtyard of the Ka‘bah • Those Who Came to Listen in Secret at Night • What They Knew, and What They Said • A Cloth Twisted Around the Neck

blocks.1: In the previous lesson we saw what Quraysh had tried. They threatened, they tempted, they mocked. They went to his uncle three times. They offered compromise, they even asked him to touch an idol just once.
blocks.2: Nothing worked. Now they took the last road. Laying hands. But there was an obstacle here. Abu Talib was still alive, Banu Hashim stood behind him. If they killed the Prophet {{1}}, a tribal war would break out, and the trade of Makkah would stop.
blocks.3: So they found a way by which pain could be inflicted, yet no account of blood would arise. The name of that way was humiliation. The mark of a beating dries up in a few days. But the man who is made a laughing-stock before a crowd, what does he go home with in the evening!
blocks.4: They did not want to beat him. They wanted people to see him and laugh. And while laughing, to forget his message. These three steps are the same in every age. One who cannot be beaten by argument is made a laughing-stock. And if even that does not work, a hand is raised against him.
blocks.5: In the noon we are going to hear about today, all three steps were present together. And one thing needs to be said first. Today’s discussion is about one man only; what came down upon the Prophet {{1}} himself. What happened to his companions was harder still. Bilal, Sumayyah, Yasir, Khabbab; that discussion is in the next lesson.
blocks.6: The torture upon the Companions was of the body. And upon him it was of humiliation. The first sheds blood. The second does not shed blood; it wears the inside away. The clearest picture of that wearing away is found in one noon.
blocks.7: That Noon in the Courtyard of the Ka‘bah
blocks.8: That day the stones of the courtyard of the Ka‘bah were heated in the sun. The Prophet {{1}} came, and came and stood before the Ka‘bah. The Ka‘bah then was their place too. Here their assembly sits, here they spend most of the day.
blocks.9: He could have stood inside the house too. No one would see, no one would say anything. He stood right here. He raised both his hands. Then folded them. And began to recite. No one stood behind him.
blocks.10: Alone. On one side of the courtyard sat a few men in a circle. Abu Jahl, ‘Utbah ibn Rabi‘ah, Shaybah ibn Rabi‘ah, al-Walid ibn ‘Utbah, Umayyah ibn Khalaf and ‘Uqbah ibn Abi Mu‘ayt.
blocks.11: None of these was an outsider. These were people of his own city. For forty years it was they who called him by the name al-Amin. When going away, it was they who left their most precious thing with him, and slept in peace.
blocks.12: He did not look at them even once. Nearby a camel had been slaughtered that day. The entrails lay on the ground. Abu Jahl looked once at that, once at the man at prayer. Then he said to his companions, which of you will bring those entrails and place them on Muhammad’s back when he prostrates!
blocks.13: The most wretched man among them stood up. ‘Uqbah ibn Abi Mu‘ayt. He lifted the thing in both hands. Then went and stood behind him. He does not know who is standing behind him.
blocks.14: He was then reciting. On one side of the courtyard a young man was standing. He saw everything. He knew what would happen now. But he had no tribe behind him. In Makkah there was not one person to speak on his behalf.
blocks.15: Had he stepped forward he would have been finished within that very crowd. And the burden would still have remained on that back. This much he knew. His feet did not move. The Prophet {{1}} went into ruku‘.
blocks.16: He rose from ruku‘. Then knelt, and placed his forehead on the ground. It was for this very moment that the man had been standing all this time. He came forward. In both his hands that thing from inside the camel’s belly. Entrails, with blood and dung wrapped around them; a whole burden.
blocks.17: He raised the thing above his head. Then dropped it between the two shoulders of the Prophet {{1}}.{{2}}
blocks.18: The burden fell on the back. And that man’s forehead was then on the ground. The courtyard filled with the sound of laughter. The leaders of Quraysh were collapsing against one another. He remained in prostration. He did not lift his head.
blocks.19: The courtyard that day was not short of people. No one stepped forward. Then through the crowd one came running. The daughter of the Prophet {{1}}, Fatimah (RA). She was then a little girl.
blocks.20: She removed the thing from her father’s back. Then turned to face those men, and began to scold them. The voice of a child, and before her the power of all Makkah.
blocks.21: The prayer ended. The Prophet {{1}} stood up. He raised both hands toward the sky. Three times he said, O Allah, seize Quraysh. Then he said, naming them one by one; Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, ‘Utbah ibn Rabi‘ah, Shaybah ibn Rabi‘ah, al-Walid ibn ‘Utbah, Umayyah ibn Khalaf, ‘Uqbah ibn Abi Mu‘ayt.
blocks.22: The laughter stopped. They knew; in this city this supplication is accepted. Many years later. The Battle of Badr is over. The bodies are being dragged from the field and thrown into an old well. And standing beside the well is that same young man.
blocks.23: He is counting. Not one is missing. The young man’s name is ‘Abdullah ibn Mas‘ud (RA). That noon he carried all his life. In old age, telling the incident, he said, and I stood there watching; if I had had even a little strength, I would have thrown it off the back of the Messenger of Allah {{1}}.{{2}}
blocks.24: That day he could not step forward; that was not his sin. Islam does not give anyone a burden beyond his capacity.
blocks.26: So fear Allah as much as you are able.{{1}}
blocks.27: The Prophet {{1}} himself stated the rule. When you see wrong, change it with your hand; if you lack the ability, with your tongue; if you cannot even do that, hate it with your heart. That day his hand was not there. His tongue was not there either.
blocks.28: The heart was there. Allah asks of no one anything beyond his capacity. Whether the work was in the end accomplished or not, He does not look at that. He looks at whether the person did as much as he could.
blocks.29: The man who shed tears all his life for being unable, did not go to Allah empty-handed. That very weeping is his deed. Those whose names were taken that day, in their hands were wealth, manpower, honour; everything.
blocks.30: And the one who had raised his hands, in his hands there was nothing. The Prophet {{1}} said, fear the supplication of the wronged; between it and Allah there is no veil.{{2}}
blocks.31: Islam has not only taught forgiving. It has also taught resisting the oppressor’s oppression. That day he could not resist with his hand. So he made supplication. Yet he did not say this either, if there is no guidance, destroy them. He invoked straight against them; the chance of their reform he left in Allah’s hand alone.
blocks.32: But cursing was not his habit. In his whole life he made such a supplication only a countable few times; on the day at Ta’if when his shoes filled with blood he did not either. The lesson is not that you may curse whomever you like. The lesson is that when nothing else is left in your hands, one hand still remains.
blocks.33: Those Who Came to Listen in Secret at Night
blocks.34: The daytime incident is done. Now a night incident. Three great men of Makkah. Abu Jahl, Abu Sufyan and al-Akhnas ibn Shariq. All three in the daytime opposed the Prophet {{1}}, sat in assemblies talking about him, and kept people away from him.
blocks.35: One night all three came out of their houses. No one told anyone. Makkah had fallen asleep. No one on the road. Each went and chose a hiding place near the house of the Prophet {{1}} and sat down.
blocks.36: Inside, he was then reciting the Qur’an in the night prayer. They began to listen. All night. The words they dismiss in the daytime as lies, sitting in the dark of night they were swallowing those very words.
blocks.37: Before dawn each rose in his own way. And on the way back the three met. All three were stunned. One began blaming another; what are you doing here! Then they promised, they would never come again. If anyone saw them, what would people think!
blocks.38: What happened the next night! All three came again. Listened all night again. Met again on the way back. Promised again. The third night the same thing. This time, annoyed with themselves, they swore, never again.{{1}}
blocks.39: In the morning al-Akhnas went to Abu Sufyan. He asked, tell me truly, what do you think! Abu Sufyan said, by Allah, I have heard some things that I understand; and some things that I do not understand.
blocks.40: Then al-Akhnas went to Abu Jahl. He asked the same question. And what Abu Jahl said lifted the veil on the whole matter. He said, we and Banu ‘Abd Manaf competed for honour. They fed people, we fed too. They gave mounts, we gave too. They gave charity, we gave too.
blocks.41: When we became equal to equal, they said, among us there is a prophet; news comes to him from the sky. Then he said, now where would we get this!
blocks.42: By Allah, we will never believe him. The man had listened to the Qur’an for three nights. He did not say, the words are false. He did not say, the man is a deceiver. Not a single argument could he show.
blocks.43: He said, this thing did not come to our house. The whole opposition stood on this one sentence. The truth was not their problem. The problem was the one in whose house the truth had descended.
blocks.44: The man sat for a long time with the paper in hand. He knows what is written inside. The interest calculation he himself worked out. He knows the thing is not right. Then he picked up the pen.
blocks.45: Signing and coming out he told himself, for now this much; we will see later. Abu Jahl too had gone home after hearing the Qur’an three nights. The pain of not knowing and the pain of knowing and not accepting are not the same thing.
blocks.46: In the first there is an excuse before Allah. In the second there is not. This man exists even today. At three at night he sits alone and listens to a talk. His eyes grow wet. He decides, from tomorrow I will change.
blocks.47: And when morning comes everything goes on as before. That night’s weeping is not worthless. It is a call from Allah’s side. Abu Jahl heard the call, then arrogance turned him back. ‘Umar (RA) too heard the same call, and he opened the door.
blocks.48: The difference is not in hearing; it is in responding.
blocks.49: What They Knew, and What They Said
blocks.50: The matter becomes clearer in another incident. It has come in a narration that Abu Jahl once said to the Prophet {{1}} to his face, we do not call you a liar. We deny what you have brought.{{2}}
blocks.51: What his face was like on hearing it no one wrote down. But it was felt in the heavens.
blocks.53: We certainly know that what they say grieves you. They do not call you a liar; rather the wrongdoers deny the verses of Allah themselves.{{1}}
blocks.54: Read the beginning of the verse once. Before answering the enemy, Allah comforted his heart. He did not say, pay no attention to their words. He said, I know the word has struck you.
blocks.55: The one whom the whole city had left alone, the heavens did not let him be alone. And then the real thing was said. They do not call you a liar. The man whom the whole city had called al-Amin for forty years cannot suddenly be made a liar. People will not believe it.
blocks.56: So they let go of the man and took hold of the message. Their problem was not with proof. Proof they had seen; they had even listened secretly in the darkness of night. Their problem was that accepting meant giving something up.
blocks.57: Accepting meant the idol trade would go. The power of custodianship of the Ka‘bah would go. They would have to say with their own mouths that the path of the fathers was wrong. And the biggest thing, they would have to bow their heads to Banu Hashim.
blocks.58: They had recognised the truth. Only the price of truth was beyond their capacity. Man does not always deny the truth without knowing. Often he does it knowingly; because if he accepts, something will go out of his hand.
blocks.59: The shopkeeper argues a great deal in the assembly. As soon as anyone raises a ruling on business he asks for evidence. Then he raises questions about the chain of the evidence. Then he says, the scholars themselves are not of one view.
blocks.60: At the end of the assembly everyone thinks, the man has studied a good deal. But on the way home he calculates how many taka a month he would lose if he gave the thing up. His question is not about the evidence.
blocks.61: The question is about that money. Man does not always deny the truth without knowing. Often he does it knowingly; because if he accepts, something will go out of his hand.
blocks.62: A Cloth Twisted Around the Neck
blocks.63: That same ‘Uqbah ibn Abi Mu‘ayt on another day went one step further. The Prophet {{1}} was standing praying beside the Ka‘bah. ‘Uqbah came from behind and wound his own cloak around his neck. Then pulled hard.
blocks.64: The cloth sank into the neck. He did not let go. That day too there were people in the courtyard. They were watching a man’s breath being cut off. No one moved. Then from afar one came running.
blocks.65: Abu Bakr (RA). He did not calculate; who is watching, who is sitting there, what will this cost tomorrow morning. He just ran. Seizing ‘Uqbah’s shoulder he pushed him away. Then he said, will you kill a man only because he says, my Lord is Allah!{{1}}
blocks.66: That day many stood there. Everyone was watching. One stepped forward. And the price of this stepping forward he had to pay. It has come in a narration that on another day, trying to save the Prophet {{1}} in just this way, he fell into the hands of Quraysh.
blocks.67: They surrounded him. ‘Utbah ibn Rabi‘ah began to strike his face with a shoe. Striking and striking until the face became so that it could not be recognised. He lay unconscious.
blocks.68: People of his tribe came and picked him up and carried him away. Everyone thought he would not live. All day his consciousness did not return. Toward evening he opened his eyes.
blocks.69: And the first word that came out of his mouth was not about his own pain. He said, how is the Messenger of Allah {{1}}!{{2}}
blocks.70: His mother brought food. He turned his face away. He said, first tell me how he is. His mother said, I do not know, my son. He said, then I will eat nothing.
blocks.71: Whose own face was then unrecognisable, his worry was for another’s face. Many years later, near the farewell, the Prophet {{1}} stood on the pulpit and said, of all people, the one who has favoured me most with his companionship and his wealth is Abu Bakr.{{2}}
blocks.72: That companionship had begun on a day when standing beside him meant staking one’s own life. On what do our friendships stand! A tea stall, a phone screen, and some laughter and jokes.
blocks.73: When everyone stands against one man, how many of our friends push through the crowd and come forward! And when did we ourselves last run for anyone!

footnotes.0: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith nos. 240, 520 and 3185; Sahih Muslim, hadith no. 1794; via ‘Abdullah ibn Mas‘ud (RA); he himself was an eyewitness of the incident. In the text of al-Bukhari 520 the description of the thing has the words ‘sala’ (the membrane and entrails inside the camel’s belly) and ‘farth wa dam’ (dung and blood). The wording of the hadith is ‘fanba‘atha ashqahum’, that is, the most wretched of them got up. At the end of the narration is his testimony that he saw every one of those named killed at Badr. In the hadith there was also the name of a seventh man, but the narrator could not recall it.
footnotes.1: Sahih Muslim, hadith no. 1794; the words of ‘Abdullah ibn Mas‘ud (RA) himself: ‘wa ana qa’imun anzuru, law kanat li mana‘atun tarahtuhu ‘an zahri Rasulillahi {{1}}.’ Here the word ‘mana‘ah’ means tribal strength and shelter; in Arabia, without it, to lay a hand on anyone was to invite one’s own death. Before accepting Islam he had been the shepherd of ‘Uqbah ibn Abi Mu‘ayt’s goats (Musnad Ahmad, hadith no. 4412; chain hasan, verification: Shu‘ayb al-Arna’ut); one reason for his helplessness that day lies here.
footnotes.3: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith no. 1496; Sahih Muslim, hadith no. 19; via Ibn ‘Abbas (RA), the hadith of sending Mu‘adh (RA) to Yemen.
footnotes.4: Ibn Ishaq; Sirat Ibn Hisham, 1/315–316. On Abu Jahl, Abu Sufyan and al-Akhnas ibn Shariq secretly listening to the Qur’an at night. The narration is of the Seerah books; the chain is mursal. It is not in Sahih al-Bukhari or Muslim. Acceptable as a scene, not as proof.
footnotes.5: Jami‘ al-Tirmidhi, hadith no. 3064; via ‘Ali (RA). ⚠ This chain has been called weak; but through other than ‘Ali’s (RA) name the narration is comparatively stronger, and al-Hakim called it sahih according to the condition of al-Bukhari and Muslim. In the lesson it is safer to take it saying ‘it has come in a narration’. The verse, however, is definitive.
footnotes.7: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith nos. 3856 and 3678; via ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr (RA). The sentence quoted by Abu Bakr (RA) is part of verse 28 of Surah Ghafir; the words of a man in the household of Pharaoh who kept his faith hidden, who could not stay silent on the day of the decision to kill Musa (AS).
footnotes.8: ⚠ This incident is not in the sahih hadith books. It is narrated in the Seerah books and al-Bazzar’s Musnad via Ibn Ishaq; Ibn Kathir has mentioned it in al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah (3/30). There is discussion among the hadith scholars about the chain, and many have called it weak. So it is used not as proof of creed or ruling but only as a scene. In the lesson it is told saying ‘it has come in a narration’. The incident of winding the cloak around the neck in the courtyard of the Ka‘bah is separate from this, and that is in Sahih al-Bukhari (hadith no. 3856).
footnotes.9: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith no. 3654; via Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri (RA). Original text: ‘inna amanna al-nasi ‘alayya fi suhbatihi wa malihi Abu Bakr.’

quiz.q: According to the lesson, what is the main difference between the torture upon the Prophet ﷺ and the torture upon the Companions?
o: One happened in Makkah, the other after going to Madinah
His was mainly of humiliation, theirs of the body
One happened openly, the other in secret
One lasted a few days, the other many years
quiz.e: The first does not shed blood; it wears the inside away. If these two are mixed up, neither is understood properly, so the torture of the Companions is in a separate lesson.

quiz.q: Why did Quraysh choose the way of humiliation instead of outright killing?
o: They had been somewhat influenced by his words
They did not want to spoil the sanctity of the Ka‘bah
They feared Abu Bakr and Hamzah (RA)
The fear of a tribal war breaking out with Banu Hashim
quiz.e: They sought a way by which pain could be inflicted yet no account of blood arose. The name of that way is humiliation; not striking, but disgracing.

quiz.q: What does the lesson say to remember about those who laugh today?
o: All kinds of relations with them should be cut off
Every word of theirs must be answered back
Invoking against them is the thing to do
‘Umar (RA) too was once in their group
quiz.e: The Prophet ﷺ did not cut relations with Abu Lahab and announce it; he kept kinship, and carried on the work too. Those who laugh today may stand by your side tomorrow.

quiz.q: If people at home mock religiousness, what does the lesson say to do?
o: Hold on to religion, and not let go of the hand of the people at home either
It is better to leave home and go to a religious environment
To reduce talking with them
To hide one’s deeds in front of them
quiz.e: The ones who hurt the Prophet ﷺ most were his own tribe, his own uncle, his own neighbour. Yet he kept kinship and carried on the work.

quiz.q: Who placed the camel’s entrails on the back of the Prophet ﷺ in prostration in the courtyard of the Ka‘bah?
o: Umayyah ibn Khalaf, who was rolling with laughter
‘Uqbah ibn Abi Mu‘ayt, the most wretched of the group
Abu Jahl, who had made the proposal that day
‘Utbah ibn Rabi‘ah, one of the leaders of the assembly
quiz.e: The Companion narrator identified him in one word; the most wretched. The proposal was made by Abu Jahl, and the deed was done by ‘Uqbah ibn Abi Mu‘ayt.

quiz.q: Who made the proposal that day to bring the entrails and place them on his back?
o: ‘Uqbah ibn Abi Mu‘ayt, who later did the deed
Shaybah ibn Rabi‘ah, one of the seated leaders
al-Walid ibn ‘Utbah, who was present in the assembly
Abu Jahl, he was the one who raised it
quiz.e: Looking once at the entrails and once at the man at prayer, Abu Jahl said, which of you will bring that and place it on his back when he prostrates!

quiz.q: Why did the Prophet ﷺ not raise his head even after the filth was placed in prostration?
o: Because he did not notice the incident
Because he wanted to avoid the laughter of Quraysh
Because raising the head would have broken the prayer
Because he was waiting for Abu Bakr (RA) to come
quiz.e: He could have stood up, could have shaken it off; but then the prayer would have broken. He took the humiliation; he did not leave the prayer.

quiz.q: What is the main lesson of the lesson from that act of Fatimah (RA)?
o: For the wronged, not the solution but companionship is the greatest
The young too should lay a hand to the work of elders
Troubles inside the family cannot be told outside
It is possible to melt the heart of the oppressor with tears
quiz.e: She could not stop Quraysh, nor did the torture stop. But that day the father learned that he was not alone. Doing as much as one has in hand is the duty.

quiz.q: When, as a victim of injustice, nothing is left in one’s hands, which door does the lesson recall?
o: Going and standing before influential men of society
Bearing patiently and forgetting the whole affair
Standing firm to claim one’s rights
The supplication of the wronged; between which and Allah there is no veil
quiz.e: The Prophet ﷺ said, fear the supplication of the wronged; between it and Allah there is no veil. The result of that supplication in the courtyard of the Ka‘bah was seen on the field of Badr.

quiz.q: What caution came in the lesson about invoking against anyone?
o: He did so very rarely; he did not at Ta’if
Only scholars can make such a supplication
Such a supplication can be made only in the month of Ramadan
It is known that such a supplication is never accepted
quiz.e: Cursing was not his habit. The lesson is not that you may curse whomever you like; the lesson is that even when nothing is left in the hand, one hand remains.

quiz.q: What is the practical resolve of this lesson?
o: To stand by someone whose suffering everyone sees
To read at least one page of the Seerah every day
To begin good conduct toward the neighbour
To send durood at least once every day
quiz.e: No need to solve it; just go and stand beside him once. Fatimah (RA) did just that.

quiz.q: Which three of Quraysh used to come to listen to the Qur’an secretly in the dark of night?
o: Abu Jahl, Abu Sufyan and al-Akhnas ibn Shariq
Abu Lahab, ‘Uqbah ibn Abi Mu‘ayt and al-Hakam
Ubayy ibn Khalaf, Umayyah and al-‘As ibn Wa’il
al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, al-Nadr and al-Harith ibn Qays
quiz.e: The three came separately on three nights and listened all night, and each time, meeting on the way back, were ashamed and promised not to come again.

quiz.q: In reply to al-Akhnas’s question, what did Abu Jahl give as the real reason for opposition?
o: The words of the Qur’an seemed meaningless to him
Muhammad had told them lies
Competition for honour with Banu ‘Abd Manaf
He could not bear the insult to the idols
quiz.e: He said, we became equal to equal in everything; now they say there is a prophet in their house. Where would we get this! The reason for the whole opposition came out in this one sentence.

quiz.q: What can be understood from the three men’s coming back again and again for three nights?
o: Truth was pulling within, arrogance was holding back
They had secretly accepted Islam
They wanted to keep secret watch on the Prophet ﷺ
They wanted to learn the language of the Qur’an
quiz.e: Each night they would swear and go back, and the next night come again. The voice they kept suppressed in the daytime was what pulled them at night.

quiz.q: What advice does the lesson give to the man who weeps sitting alone at night and forgets everything in the morning?
o: First to take the big decisions of life
Not to leave it till morning but to do one small deed
To go to a scholar and tell him everything
To take care that no one notices the weeping
quiz.e: Abu Jahl heard the call, then arrogance turned him back; ‘Umar (RA) heard the same call and opened the door. The difference is in responding.

quiz.q: When ‘Uqbah wound his cloak around the neck of the praying Prophet ﷺ and pulled, who came forward?
o: Hamzah (RA), who was nearby
Abu Bakr (RA), running from afar
‘Umar (RA), pushing through the crowd
Abu Talib, in charge of his nephew’s safety
quiz.e: Abu Bakr (RA) came running from afar, seized ‘Uqbah’s shoulder and pushed him away. Many were standing there; one stepped forward.

quiz.q: ‘Will you kill a man only because he says, my Lord is Allah!’ — which surah of the Qur’an is this verse?
o: Surah al-An‘am, a verse on patience against denial
Surah al-Hijr, a verse on the mockers
Surah al-‘Alaq, a verse on the one who obstructs
Surah Ghafir, the words of the believer in Pharaoh’s household
quiz.e: The sentence Abu Bakr (RA) spoke is part of verse 28 of Surah Ghafir; in the story of Musa (AS), the words of a believer in Pharaoh’s household.

quiz.q: What lesson does the lesson draw from Abu Bakr’s (RA) act that day?
o: Arguing with the oppressor is the most important thing
One person is enough to stand beside the wronged
Every wrong must be answered at once
One must advance only with the leaders’ permission
quiz.e: At that moment many were standing there; one stepped forward. He gave no speech, gathered no party; he removed the hand and spoke one sentence.

porbos.title: Neighbours at the House Door • The Path Strewn with Thorns • The Jab That Cuts the Deepest • He Never Took Revenge for Himself • Those Who Took Up the Work of Mockery • And What the Rest of Makkah Was Doing • The Friend Who Pulls You Down

blocks.1: However much pain a man suffers outside all day, in the evening he returns home. The house is his last shelter. Entering it and shutting the door, the laughter and mockery of outside can no longer come in.
blocks.2: They did not spare even that door of his. The names of those who lived around the house of the Prophet {{1}} were these. Abu Lahab, his own uncle. ‘Uqbah ibn Abi Mu‘ayt. al-Hakam ibn Abi al-‘As. And ‘Adi ibn Hamra’.
blocks.3: By the custom of Arabia the standing of a neighbour was the highest. To hurt a neighbour was the greatest shame; it made the face of the whole tribe small. They gave up even that shame.
blocks.4: Cooking had been put on at the house. After a whole day the people of the house would eat. Filth from outside fell into the pot. One day the entrails of a goat were thrown into that cooking vessel.
blocks.5: He took it up on the end of a stick. Then went and stood at the door. And said, O Banu ‘Abd Manaf, what kind of neighbourliness is this!{{1}}
blocks.6: That much only. Then he went back. He did not abuse anyone by name. He did not curse. He did not go inside and sit sulking either. He simply held up their own values before them; you do know the standing of a neighbour.
blocks.7: And this very man later said, Jibril advised me so much about the neighbour that I thought the neighbour would surely be made an heir. The one who tasted the pain from neighbours most, by his hand the rights of the neighbour were written.
blocks.8: For four years the man has lived in that flat. On the stairs he meets the person from the next door every day. They nod their heads and go off in two directions. One morning seeing a crowd downstairs he asked, what has happened.
blocks.9: Someone said, the man on the third floor died in the night. Standing at the funeral prayer he heard that man’s name for the first time. A camel’s belly none of us throws into anyone’s pot. But the chips packet we throw down from the window, which falls into the neighbour’s yard.
blocks.10: Sweeping our own veranda we push the dirt toward his boundary. We park the car so that it blocks his gate. At one at night we play loud music, not thinking whether someone is sleeping on the other side of the wall.
blocks.11: The small filth we throw every day; we do not even notice. And the big question remains; in the next house the person is alive, or not.
blocks.13: The work of causing pain was not done by men alone. The name of Abu Lahab’s wife was Arwa; she was called Umm Jamil. She was the sister of Abu Sufyan, a girl of the most distinguished house of Quraysh.
blocks.14: In the daytime, seeing her, eyes could not be turned away. She walked the roads of Makkah wearing gold jewellery, and people moved aside to make way. And when night fell she went out.
blocks.15: In the darkness she gathered thorns. Then carrying them on her shoulder she spread them on that path along which a man would walk in the morning.{{1}}
blocks.16: That man would go out to give da‘wah. The hand that should have gathered honour, that hand gathered thorns. Where enmity brings a person down! The Qur’an wrote her description for ever.
blocks.18: And his wife too, who carries firewood. Around her neck will be a twisted rope.{{1}}
blocks.19: No one remembered the gold jewellery. They remembered that burden on the shoulder. And the Prophet {{1}} never said even one word to her. He did not change the path, he did not protest. Clearing away the thorns he walked on.
blocks.20: The one on whose path thorns were spread every day is the one who told us, faith has more than seventy branches; the highest of them is La ilaha illa Allah, and the lowest is removing a harmful thing from the road.{{1}}
blocks.21: He did not say this from the pages of a book. He said it from beneath his own feet. Leaving the car at the mouth of the narrow lane the man went into the shop. Two minutes’ work. Behind, a rickshaw got stuck. Then another. The lane filled with the sound of horns.
blocks.22: An old man, trying to get past the car, slipped at the edge of the drain and sat down. The man was then standing in the shop settling the price. He does not even know what has happened outside.
blocks.23: Umm Jamil spread the thorns out of enmity. And we spread them absent-mindedly. The name of the one who left hardship on the path the Qur’an has kept written.
blocks.24: The Jab That Cuts the Deepest
blocks.25: Not all blows are equal. Some blows strike the body. And some strike a place where the hand does not reach. The sons of the Prophet {{1}} had gone in infancy. Qasim went. ‘Abdullah went too.
blocks.26: What it is inside a father’s chest then, only fathers know. And right at that place Quraysh placed a finger. In Arabia lineage was the greatest wealth. For one with no son, his name would be erased; this was their belief. Such a man they called abtar, cut-off.
blocks.27: Al-‘As ibn Wa’il said, leave him; he is abtar. When he dies his name is finished.{{1}}
blocks.28: They said this laughing. Standing before a grieving father. The reply came from the heavens; in just three verses.
blocks.30: Indeed We have given you al-Kawthar. So pray to your Lord, and sacrifice. Indeed it is your enemy who is cut off.{{1}}
blocks.31: It was not said that you will have a son. It was said, you have been given al-Kawthar. And the one who jabbed you, cut off is he. Fourteen hundred years have passed. Where the lineage of al-‘As ibn Wa’il is, no one knows.
blocks.32: And every day millions of people send durood with a name; it is the name of that very man who was called abtar. Twelve years of marriage have passed, the man’s house is still empty. Sitting in an assembly, someone or other brings it up.
blocks.33: Well, any good news! Someone says with a laugh, get the treatment done too; or will you marry again! Everyone laughs. He laughs too. What else can one do but laugh; if he did not laugh it would seem he cannot bear it.
blocks.34: Then when the assembly breaks up he is the first to rise. Returning home he sits quiet for a long time. Those who said it forgot it that very night. The reply to Quraysh’s jab came from the heavens.
blocks.35: Who will give the reply to our jabs!
blocks.36: He Never Took Revenge for Himself
blocks.37: After all that what did he do! The man who put entrails on his back. The one who twisted the cloth around his neck. The one who threw filth into the cooking pot. The one who laughed over his dead child.
blocks.38: Eight years later he returned to Makkah. This time power in his hand. The city beneath his feet. And those who had hurt him standing before him. He did not ask for even one account.
blocks.39: ‘A’ishah (RA) saw him from the closest. She says, the Messenger of Allah {{1}} never took revenge for himself; only when the limits of Allah were violated he would take action for Allah.{{2}}
blocks.40: Never for himself. Always for Allah. Without understanding the difference between these two, the religion cannot be understood. And we do exactly the opposite; at our own insult we become fire, and when Allah’s right is lost we stay silent.
blocks.41: The one who was wronged most, he took the least revenge. Forgiveness was not his weakness. Forgiveness was his strength; because he forgave while power was in his hand.
blocks.42: The case has been running for seven years. The cost has long since exceeded the value of the land. The lawyer had said, settle it; there is no profit. The man had said, I am not fighting for the money. I am fighting for what he said to me before everyone.
blocks.43: That one remark he has carried for seven years. Yet in that same assembly the day someone mocked the religion, he laughed and changed the subject. For his own insult, seven years.
blocks.44: For Allah’s right, not even seven seconds. The one who was wronged most, getting power in his hand, did not ask for even one account. This week forgive one person whom you have the power to punish.
blocks.45: Without power one cannot forgive; that is called helplessness.
blocks.46: Those Who Took Up the Work of Mockery
blocks.47: In Makkah there was a group of people whose whole work was mockery. They did not beat. They laughed. Wherever the Prophet {{1}} stood, they went and stood. He recited the Qur’an, they made faces. He sat, they winked and signalled. People burst into laughter, and the word was no longer heard.
blocks.48: In the narrations of the Seerah the names of five of this group have come. al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib, al-Aswad ibn ‘Abd Yaghuth, al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, al-‘As ibn Wa’il and al-Harith ibn Qays.{{1}}
blocks.49: None of these was an ordinary person. They were leading men of Makkah, at whose word the bazaar would stop. And here is the real harm of mockery. In an argument you can give a reply. But for laughter there is no reply. Laughter makes the word small, and people think; then this word is not important.
blocks.50: The reply came from the heavens in one sentence.
blocks.52: Indeed, against the mockers I alone am sufficient for you.{{1}}
blocks.53: It was not said, you reply to them. It was not said, you be patient. It was said, their matter I will see to. And within a few years not one of them remained. One went by disease, one by accident, one on the field of Badr.
blocks.54: The laughter with which they wanted to stop a da‘wah, that very laughter erased their own names. The boy’s job is new. At Zuhr time he spread a sheet of paper in the empty corner and stood in prayer.
blocks.55: From behind someone said something. What was said he did not hear. He heard only the laughter. The next day at Zuhr time he looked at the clock, then pulled the file toward him. He told himself, today there is a bit more work.
blocks.56: The third day too. No one beat him. One laugh; and that was enough. That day the laughter in the courtyard of the Ka‘bah was even bigger. And the one being laughed at finished the prayer and the next day went and stood in the same place again.
blocks.57: Going the next day is the real reply. And the other side is also worth seeing. Those who laughed that day were once ordinary people too. One morning waking from sleep they did not decide, from today I will be an oppressor. It began with small laughs.
blocks.58: Today in our assemblies too, if someone mispronounces a word of the Qur’an, the whole room bursts out laughing. Someone has taken up religion, his dress is not yet in order; we exchange glances and laugh.
blocks.59: That man perhaps did not return. And we will never know which door we shut that day. The Qur’an has spoken directly on this–
blocks.61: O you who believe! Let no people mock another people; perhaps they are better than them. And let no women mock other women; perhaps they are better than them. And do not find fault with one another, and do not call one another by bad names.{{1}}
blocks.62: The one you are laughing at may be dearer to Allah than you. The people of Makkah too did not know that the one they were laughing at was the best of all creation.
blocks.63: And What the Rest of Makkah Was Doing
blocks.64: In Makkah there were not only Abu Jahl and ‘Uqbah. There were thousands of people. Where were they! They were right beside. Standing and watching. These people knew the Prophet {{1}}. They had known him forty years. They themselves called him by the name al-Amin; they used to leave their trusts in his house.
blocks.65: On the hill of Safa the day he asked, have I ever told you a lie! all Makkah said in one voice, no; we have never heard you tell a lie.{{1}}
blocks.66: The same people were now seeing filth fall on him. And were not saying a single word. One thinks, what is it to me. One thinks, when the leaders are saying nothing, who am I! One thinks, right and wrong can be seen later; first let me save my business.
blocks.67: History did not keep their names. Abu Jahl’s name is there; as a bad one, but it is there. Abu Bakr’s (RA) name is there. And of these thousands of spectators there is not even one name.
blocks.68: Silence is no neutral position. To stay silent before the oppressor is to stand beside the oppressor. Because the one being beaten sees two things. The face of the one beating, and the faces of those looking on.
blocks.69: In the class everyone together used to torment the boy. Someone hid his bag, someone called him by a distorted name. A daily matter. The rest did not laugh, nor did they stop it. They only looked on.
blocks.70: One day the boy stopped coming to school. Those who tormented, their names went into the teacher’s register. And those who looked on, no one said anything to them. They had done nothing.
blocks.71: That day in the courtyard of the Ka‘bah too thousands did nothing. And for that very reason not one of them has a name. The one being beaten sees two faces. The face of the one beating, and the faces of those looking on.
blocks.72: The Prophet {{1}} left no gap in this matter. He said, whoever among you sees a wrong, let him change it with his hand. If he lacks the ability, with his tongue. If he cannot even do that, he should hate it with his heart; and that is the weakest level of faith.
blocks.74: Hating with the heart too is a level. But the weakest level. And almost all of us are standing right there; telling ourselves, I have done nothing bad. Climbing one step up means opening the mouth. And that is never more than one sentence.
blocks.75: Abu Bakr (RA) that day gave no speech, gathered no party. Pushing through the crowd he stepped forward and removed the hand, and said one thing. For fourteen hundred years we have been telling of that one sentence of his.
blocks.76: The Friend Who Pulls You Down
blocks.77: ‘Uqbah ibn Abi Mu‘ayt has come up before. That man who twisted the cloth around his neck. But the beginning of his story is different. One day he had invited the Prophet {{1}} to his house. Listened to his words. And inside had grown soft.
blocks.78: The news reached his friend Ubayy ibn Khalaf’s ear. Ubayy came and said, you have listened to Muhammad! Your face is forbidden to me unless you go and spit on his face.{{1}}
blocks.79: A man had come as far as the door of truth. And a friendship pulled him down. He went. And did what he did. Why did he do it! Did he believe that the Prophet {{1}} was a liar!
blocks.80: No. He did it because he did not want to be small before his friend. The Qur’an has drawn the last scene of this man.
blocks.82: And on that day the wrongdoer will bite his hands; he will say, oh, if only I had taken a path with the Messenger! Oh my misfortune! If only I had not taken so-and-so as a friend! After the admonition came to me, it was he who turned me away from it.{{1}}
blocks.83: In the verse there is one word; so-and-so. The name is not given. Because in every age this so-and-so exists. And what is he lamenting! Not wealth. Not power.
blocks.84: A friendship. The friend was not an enemy. Had he been an enemy one could have been on guard. He was the person beside you; whose word cannot be put aside. Around us too there is such a one.
blocks.85: When you take up prayer he laughs. When you grow a beard he passes remarks. He does not want anything bad. He only wants the person to stay as before. And that staying as before is the biggest loss.
blocks.86: The Prophet {{1}} said, a person is upon the religion of his close friend; so look to whom you take as a friend.{{2}}
blocks.87: Today it is necessary to take stock of one’s own friends once. How many call me to the path of religion! And those who call, in which direction do they call; toward Paradise, or toward the punishment of Hellfire!
blocks.88: I am not talking about giving up friends. I am saying, make one such friend before whom you do not feel shy to do the good deed; rather you feel shy to do the bad.
blocks.89: If only ‘Uqbah had had one like that!

footnotes.1: Ibn Ishaq; Sirat Ibn Hisham. On Umm Jamil bint Harb. The narration is of the Seerah books, the chain mursal; acceptable as a scene, not as proof. The revelation of the verse of Surah Lahab in her name is in the Qur’an itself.
footnotes.3: Sahih Muslim, hadith no. 35; via Abu Hurayrah (RA). In one narration of it the full text has come: ‘fa afdaluha qawl La ilaha illa Allah, wa adnaha imatat al-adha ‘an al-tariq.’ A shortened form of the hadith is also in Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith no. 9.
footnotes.4: Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur’an al-‘Azim, tafsir of Surah al-Kawthar; on the authority of al-Bazzar and Ibn Abi Hatim, via Ibn ‘Abbas (RA). There is variation in the occasion of revelation; some name al-‘As ibn Wa’il, some ‘Uqbah or Abu Jahl. That Quraysh used to say this, the exegetes agree.
footnotes.6: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith no. 3560; Sahih Muslim, hadith no. 2327; via ‘A’ishah (RA). In the same hadith it is that when given a choice between two matters he would choose the easier one, as long as it was not a sin.
footnotes.7: Ibn Ishaq; Sirat Ibn Hisham. On ‘al-mustahzi’un’. The names are in the Seerah books; the chain is mursal, so acceptable as a scene, not as proof in creed. The verse, however, is the Qur’an’s own.
footnotes.10: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith no. 4971; via Ibn ‘Abbas (RA). The details of the incident came in the previous lesson.
footnotes.11: Sahih Muslim, hadith no. 49; via Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri (RA).
footnotes.12: Ibn Ishaq; Sirat Ibn Hisham. The exegetes too have mentioned this incident on the occasion of revelation of verses 27–29 of Surah al-Furqan. The chain of the narration is mursal; the verses, however, are the Qur’an’s.
footnotes.14: Sunan Abi Dawud, hadith no. 4833; Jami‘ al-Tirmidhi, hadith no. 2378; via Abu Hurayrah (RA). Imam al-Tirmidhi said the hadith is hasan gharib; al-Albani called it hasan.

quiz.q: Whose names came in the lesson among the neighbours around the house of the Prophet ﷺ?
o: Abu Jahl, Ubayy ibn Khalaf and al-Nadr ibn al-Harith
‘Utbah, Shaybah, al-Walid ibn ‘Utbah and Umayyah
al-‘As ibn Wa’il, al-Harith ibn Qays and al-Aswad
Abu Lahab, ‘Uqbah, al-Hakam ibn Abi al-‘As and ‘Adi
quiz.e: Abu Lahab was his own uncle. By the custom of Arabia the standing of a neighbour was the highest; they gave up even that shame.

quiz.q: When filth was thrown in the cooking vessel, what did the Prophet ﷺ say standing at the door?
o: O Banu ‘Abd Manaf, what kind of neighbourliness is this!
O Quraysh, will you not listen to me!
O Allah, You see to the matter of these!
O my uncle, do you not see all this!
quiz.e: Lifting the thing on the end of a stick he went to the door, said just this much, then went back. He did not abuse anyone by name, nor curse.

quiz.q: What was Umm Jamil’s identity?
o: Sister of Abu Jahl, a distinguished woman of Banu Makhzum
Wife of ‘Uqbah ibn Abi Mu‘ayt and a poet of Quraysh
Wife of Abu Lahab, and sister of Abu Sufyan
Daughter of Umayyah ibn Khalaf, from a rich house of Makkah
quiz.e: Her real name was Arwa; she was a girl of the most distinguished house of Quraysh. At night she would gather thorns and spread them on the path of the Prophet ﷺ.

quiz.q: By what description is Umm Jamil mentioned in the Qur’an?
o: The woman who came to listen secretly to the Qur’an in the dark of night
Hammalat al-hatab; that is, carrier of firewood
The woman who went on destroying the neighbour’s right
A woman of the most aristocratic house of Makkah
quiz.e: It comes in verses 4–5 of Surah Lahab, and his wife too, who carries firewood; around her neck will be a twisted rope. History has remembered her by that name.

quiz.q: Why did Quraysh jab the Prophet ﷺ with ‘abtar’?
o: He had withdrawn from the leadership of the tribe
Because he had denied the old customs of the lineage
He was spoiling Quraysh’s trade routes
His sons passed away in infancy
quiz.e: In Arabia the name of one with no son would be erased, this was their belief; such a man they called abtar, that is, cut-off. Qasim and ‘Abdullah had gone in infancy.

quiz.q: In reply to this jab which surah was revealed?
o: Surah al-Kawthar; the reply in just three verses
Surah Lahab; revealed concerning the uncle
Surah al-Hujurat; the verse forbidding mockery
Surah al-Furqan; the verse of the wrongdoer’s regret
quiz.e: In Surah al-Kawthar it was not said that you will have a son; it was said, you have been given al-Kawthar, and cut off is your enemy alone.

quiz.q: According to the narration of ‘A’ishah (RA), when did the Prophet ﷺ take revenge?
o: When any member of his family was hurt
When someone openly called him a liar
Only when the limits of Allah were violated, for Allah
When some wrong happened inside the mosque
quiz.e: In Sahih al-Bukhari 3560 it has come, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ never took revenge for himself; only when the limits of Allah were violated he would take action for Allah.

quiz.q: Among those whose names came in the narrations of the Seerah in the ‘group of mockers’, who was there?
o: al-Akhnas ibn Shariq and Ubayy ibn Khalaf
al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah and al-Harith ibn Qays
‘Uqbah ibn Abi Mu‘ayt and al-Hakam ibn Abi al-‘As
Abu Lahab and his wife Umm Jamil bint Harb
quiz.e: The names of five have come; al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib, al-Aswad ibn ‘Abd Yaghuth, al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, al-‘As ibn Wa’il and al-Harith ibn Qays.

quiz.q: Which verse is the reply that came from the heavens concerning the mockers?
o: Surah al-An‘am 34; the patience of earlier messengers
Surah al-Baqarah 214; Allah’s help is near
Surah al-‘Ankabut 2; they will not be left without being tested
Surah al-Hijr 95; against the mockers I am sufficient
quiz.e: It was not said that you reply to them; it was said, their matter I will see to. Within a few years not one of them remained.

quiz.q: According to the lesson why does mockery do more harm even than argument?
o: Mockery is often done in a public place
The mockers are usually more in number
An argument can be answered, there is no answer to laughter
Mockery makes people angry the most
quiz.e: Laughter makes the word small, and people think; then this word is not important. One who cannot be beaten by argument is made a laughing-stock.

quiz.q: If someone laughs at your prayer in the office, what is the biggest reply according to the lesson?
o: Point out their mistake at once
Stand in the same place again the next day
Report the matter to a superior
Change the place of prayer
quiz.e: The one who laughs does not ask you for argument; so he cannot be stopped with argument. The Prophet ﷺ went and stood in the very same place again the next day.

quiz.q: If someone mispronounces a word of the Qur’an in an assembly, or the dress of a new practising person is untidy, what does the lesson say to do?
o: Right away point out and correct the mistake in front of everyone
Evade the matter and stay silent
Swallow the laugh, and go and sit beside him
Tell the imam after the assembly ends
quiz.e: That man perhaps did not return; and we will never know which door we shut that day.

quiz.q: In verse 11 of Surah al-Hujurat, which reason is attached with the prohibition of mockery?
o: Mockery creates division in society
Perhaps they are better than them
The mockers will be humiliated on the Day of Resurrection
Mockery breaks people’s hearts
quiz.e: The one you are laughing at may be dearer to Allah than you. The people of Makkah too did not know that the one they were laughing at is the best of creation.

quiz.q: Why do people draw back at just a question of the type ‘have you become a huzur now’?
o: We fear a laugh more than death
This happens because we do not know the word of religion well
Because our faith is utterly weak
We believe our friends’ words the most
quiz.e: No one beat them, nor frightened them; only a question was thrown. Had ‘Uqbah had a good friend, that day he would have left by the other door.

quiz.q: About a good deed given up on hearing people’s words, what does the lesson say to do?
o: To do it in secret now
To avoid those people
To drop it and take up some other good deed
To start it again, and do it the next day too
quiz.e: Not once; the next day too. Going the next day is the real reply. There is only one thing that can stop him; showing that you are not stopping.

quiz.q: Why is silence before oppression not called neutrality in the lesson?
o: Because the oppressor gets courage from the silence around
Because the silent person too in time becomes an oppressor himself
Because silence increases the anger of the wronged
Because staying silent spreads disorder in society
quiz.e: The one being beaten sees two things; the face of the one beating, and the faces of those looking on. Silence makes the oppressor’s work easy.

quiz.q: Why are the names of the silent spectators of Makkah not in history, what explanation came in the lesson?
o: Because they were very few in number
Because their tribe later left Makkah
Because they did nothing on either side
Because the narrators had forgotten about them
quiz.e: Abu Jahl’s name is there, as a bad one it is there. Abu Bakr’s (RA) name is there. And of the thousands of spectators there is not one name.

quiz.q: What are the three levels about what to do on seeing wrong, which the Prophet ﷺ mentioned?
o: First supplication, then charity, finally patience
First bring witnesses, then seek judgement, finally forgiveness
With the hand, if not possible with the tongue, if not even that with the heart
First advice, then warning, finally boycott
quiz.e: Hating with the heart is called the weakest level of faith. And almost all of us are standing right there; telling ourselves, I have done nothing bad.

quiz.q: What kind of act did the lesson mention to stop today’s small oppressions?
o: Taking up a big protest programme
Stopping laughing, saying ‘leave it’, going and sitting beside
Writing down the incident and reporting later
Waiting until the authorities take action
quiz.e: We think that to stop oppression something big must be done, so we do nothing. Abu Bakr (RA) that day did nothing more than a standing and a sentence.

quiz.q: Who brought ‘Uqbah ibn Abi Mu‘ayt back from the door of truth?
o: His friend Ubayy ibn Khalaf, with a condition
Abu Jahl, calling him into the courtyard of the Ka‘bah
Umayyah ibn Khalaf, showing business accounts
al-Akhnas ibn Shariq, invoking the tribe
quiz.e: ‘Uqbah had once invited the Prophet ﷺ home, heard the words and softened. Ubayy came and said, your face is forbidden to me unless you go and spit on his face.

quiz.q: In verses 27–29 of Surah al-Furqan, what will the wrongdoer lament on the Day of Resurrection?
o: His wealth and business, which did not avail
The honour of his tribe, which was false
A friendship, which had turned him away
His power and influence, which had made him arrogant
quiz.e: He will say, oh my misfortune! If only I had not taken so-and-so as a friend! After the admonition came, it was he who turned me away from it.

quiz.q: What was the main cause of ‘Uqbah’s fall, according to the lesson?
o: He never listened to the Prophet’s ﷺ words
He did not want to be small before his friend
He had fallen into the greed of wealth
He feared losing the leadership of the tribe
quiz.e: He did not believe that the Prophet ﷺ was a liar; he did it because he did not want to be small before his friend. A friendship pulled him down from the door of truth.

quiz.q: Why, in the verse of Surah al-Furqan, is the friend called ‘so-and-so’ without his name?
o: Erasing his name was the main purpose of the verse
The name was unknown to the Arabs
To protect the honour of his lineage
Because in every age this so-and-so exists
quiz.e: See in the verse what he is lamenting; not wealth, not power, a friendship.

quiz.q: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about choosing friends?
o: Friends must be chosen by looking at tribe and lineage
A friend must always be told the truth
An account of wealth must be kept with the friend
A person is upon the religion of his friend
quiz.e: The word is said not to frighten but with calculation. With the one with whom most of the day is spent, a person slowly becomes like him.

porbos.title: The Foot That Never Advanced • The Hand That Could Never Reach • Filth on the Road, Dust on the Head • The Consolation That Came Down from the Heavens • Those Who Are Tested Most • If Allah Willed, in a Single Moment • Final Word

blocks.1: Abu Jahl one day swore an oath. He said, if I see Muhammad in prostration, I will place my foot on his neck. Or I will rub his face in the ground.
blocks.2: The people heard the statement. They waited to see what he would do. The chance came. The Prophet {{1}} stood in prayer. Abu Jahl advanced. Everyone was watching. Then suddenly he stopped.
blocks.3: He began to retreat. With both hands he made a gesture as if shielding himself. As if something were charging at him. The people asked, what happened to you! He said, I saw between me and him a trench of fire. And something terrifying. And wings.{{1}}
blocks.4: Later the Prophet {{1}} said, had he come a little further, the angels would have torn him limb from limb. And the Qur’an brought up this very man–
blocks.6: Have you seen the one who forbids a servant when he prays! ... Does he not know that Allah sees! No indeed; if he does not desist, We shall surely seize him by the forelock; a lying, sinful forelock.{{1}}
blocks.7: The man who had sworn openly drew back before the crowd. And his shame was placed in the Qur’an. He did not know that this one moment of his fear would be recited until the Day of Judgement.
blocks.8: The most powerful man of Makkah, a stone in his hand, before him an unarmed man in prostration. And he could not advance a single step. Who stopped him! Not anyone in the courtyard; everyone was just looking on.
blocks.9: What stopped him no one’s eye fell upon. The job is new, and everyone has warned about the boss’s temper. Zuhr time came. The man started to get up and sat back down.
blocks.10: He thought, today is the first week; let me settle in a bit more. The next week too the same. After six months he realised, there had been nothing to fear. In the office two others also pray; he simply did not know.
blocks.11: Six months he lost to a fear that had no existence at all. That day in the courtyard of the Ka‘bah Abu Jahl had a real stone in his hand, all Makkah behind him.
blocks.12: And he could not advance one step. The power to harm is in no one’s hand, unless Allah permits.
blocks.13: The Hand That Could Never Reach
blocks.14: That Quraysh wanted to finish him, about that there is no doubt. Remember the proposal of ‘Umarah ibn al-Walid! They told Abu Talib, take this boy; and give us your nephew, we will finish him. They did not say it secretly; they said it sitting in the assembly.
blocks.15: Abu Jahl had sworn to put a foot on his neck. ‘Uqbah had wound a cloak around his throat. The aim was one. Yet they could not. Why! The outward reason is known to all. Banu Hashim stood behind him, Abu Talib did not withdraw his hand. By the rule of Arabia to kill one man was war with the whole tribe.
blocks.16: But this argument does not explain everything. Quraysh did not fear war; they had even fought a forty-year tribal war. And the day Abu Jahl advanced with a stone in hand, no man stopped him.
blocks.17: That day what stopped him was something that no one in Makkah could see. The safety of the Prophet {{1}} did not stand on the swords of Banu Hashim. Abu Talib would go one day. Banu Hashim too would grow weak. Yet he would remain.
blocks.18: And that night, the night they would surround the house; sword in hand, one man from each tribe. That day too they would not be able. That incident will come in the lesson on the Hijrah.
blocks.19: The work that Allah wants to keep, man cannot erase. And the man whom Allah wants to keep, no hand reaches. The man could not sleep at night.
blocks.20: At the office someone is after him. Carrying tales to the big boss, holding up files. He was calculating, if the job goes how will the household run. And in just those days the money for his son’s admission came from a place he had not even looked toward.
blocks.21: Provision was not in the man’s hand. The One who is the Lord of the one whom all the power of Makkah could not touch, is your Lord too.
blocks.22: Filth on the Road, Dust on the Head
blocks.23: You have heard of the big incidents. But persecution does not happen only in big incidents. What wears away most is the small daily blows. He went out of the house. On the road someone threw filth. Someone jeered from behind. Someone stood blocking the way.
blocks.24: He sat in an assembly. People got up and left. He went to the market. Someone called out, do not listen to him; he is a sorcerer. One day dust was rubbed on his head. In that very state he returned home.
blocks.25: The girl came running, brought water and began to wash his head. And while washing she began to weep. He said, daughter, do not weep. Allah will protect your father.{{1}}
blocks.26: The girl weeps for her father. And the father consoles the girl. He did not once speak of his own pain. In these days not once did he strike back. Not once did he curse anyone; except that one day, the day filth was placed on him in prostration. And even that day he asked nothing for himself.
blocks.27: And the hardship was not only of humiliation. It was of hunger too. Many years later he himself said, no one has been hurt in the way of Allah as I have been hurt. And thirty days and nights have passed over me when for me and Bilal there was no food that any living creature could eat; only so little as could be hidden under Bilal’s armpit.{{1}}
blocks.28: Thirty days. And what food there was, was no more than a handful. The girl in her in-laws’ house does not endure any great torment. No one beats her. No one stops her rice either.
blocks.29: Only every day there is a remark about the cooking. When her parents’ home comes up someone gives a little laugh. Going to a function she is called last of all. Each incident so small that it cannot even be told to anyone. If told people will say, is that all!
blocks.30: After three years the smile disappeared from the girl’s face. Under a big blow a person stands firm. He breaks down under the small daily blows. And his hardship was not only of humiliation.
blocks.31: If a meal is late by a single time we shout in the house. His thirty days passed on food that was no more than a handful.
blocks.32: The Consolation That Came Down from the Heavens
blocks.33: In these days he was not left alone. After each blow something would come down from the heavens. Sometimes it was acknowledgement. Allah would say, I know your chest is tightening.
blocks.35: And We certainly know that your heart is constricted by what they say. So glorify the praise of your Lord, and be among those who prostrate. And worship your Lord until the certainty comes to you.{{1}}
blocks.36: What could the medicine have been! A settlement with them, or going away for some time. It was said, go to prostration. To that very prostration in which he had been humiliated, he was told to return. Because from the place where the blow lands, the strength too comes from there.
blocks.37: Sometimes it was a command to patience.
blocks.39: And be patient over what they say; and withdraw from them in a beautiful manner.{{1}}
blocks.40: Sabr, and withdrawing beautifully. Not quarrel, not revenge; and not giving up either. And sometimes it was reminding him of the earlier prophets.
blocks.42: And messengers before you were denied; yet they were patient over the denial and the hurt, until My help came to them.{{1}}
blocks.43: In the verses nowhere is it said that the hardship will be lifted. It is said, help will come. And until the help comes there is only one thing to do; sabr. Here the real meaning of sabr comes out. Sabr does not mean silently enduring. Sabr means carrying on the work without stopping it.
blocks.44: Even with filth on him the next day he went and stood again in the courtyard of the Ka‘bah. That is sabr. That day the man rolled up his prayer mat and put it away. For about six months he had been making supplication for one thing. It had not happened.
blocks.45: He told himself, there is no gain in asking. Then the days came on even heavier. Because earlier there was at least one place where one could go and lighten the heart; now even that is gone.
blocks.46: To him too it was not said that the hardship would be lifted. It was said, glorify, and be with those who prostrate. On the day nothing is going right, that very day the prayer mat is needed most.
blocks.47: That place is the one place where, even if no one listens to you, One listens.
blocks.49: Here a question naturally arises. Allah loves him. Then why so much hardship! The question is not new. The Companions too asked; who among people is tested most severely!
blocks.50: He said, the prophets. Then those nearest to them. Then those nearest to them. And then he stated the rule. A person is tested according to his religion; the stronger one is in religion, the harder his test.{{1}}
blocks.51: Turned over, the matter is like this. We think, hardship means Allah has turned His face away. And he is saying, exactly the opposite. The nearer one is, the bigger his test. The prophets suffered most.
blocks.52: And among the prophets who suffered most he himself told with his own mouth; that came in the previous section. Since the boy took up religion his life has become hard.
blocks.53: Unrest at home. Friends have moved away. The job that had almost happened did not happen either. One day he blurted out, this never used to happen before. Has Allah become displeased with me!
blocks.54: The question is not his alone. And the hadith says exactly the opposite. The nearer one is, the bigger his test. The prophets got the most. But one thing. Suffering hardship is in itself no credit.
blocks.55: The credit is standing firm within the hardship.
blocks.56: If Allah Willed, in a Single Moment
blocks.57: Arriving at this point the heart asks a question. If Allah willed He could have stopped everything in a single moment. He could have seized Abu Jahl’s hand. He could have given faith to all of Makkah.
blocks.60: And if your Lord had willed, all who are on the earth would have believed.{{1}}
blocks.61: Then why did He not stop it! The answer is in the Qur’an too.
blocks.63: Do people think that they will be left alone because they say, we have believed, and not be tested!{{1}}
blocks.64: The test is no accident. The test is part of the system itself. And there is another verse, reading which makes the chest tremble.
blocks.66: Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while there has not yet come to you the like of those who passed before you! Poverty and hardship afflicted them, and they were shaken so much that the Messenger and those who believed with him said, when will Allah’s help come! Listen, Allah’s help is near.{{1}}
blocks.67: Who asked the question! Not ordinary people. The Messenger and the believers with him. That means asking this question is not a sin. When will the help come! This word has come from the mouths of prophets too.
blocks.68: The sin is asking the question and stopping. And the last word of the verse. Allah did not say, help will come. He said, help is near. At the moment when it seems one can bear no more, at exactly that moment the help is nearest.
blocks.69: Those thirteen years of Makkah are the proof. The day he stood alone in the courtyard of the Ka‘bah, no one thought that this man’s name would one day be proclaimed from inside this very Ka‘bah.
blocks.70: The help was near even then. It was just not seen. Two brothers started business together. In the first year itself money came into one’s hand; no hardship had to be endured. The other spent seven years on debts and changing shops.
blocks.71: Ten years later the first one’s business is no more. In one blow everything went. And the second still stands; because he knows which blow is to be handled how.
blocks.72: What comes easily, goes easily too. A faith that has not passed any test breaks down at the first blow. And a supplication not being accepted and being accepted late are not the same thing.
blocks.73: The Prophet {{1}} said, whatever hardship befalls a Muslim, even a thorn pricking him, Allah erases sins in exchange for it.{{2}}
blocks.74: The account of even one thorn is kept. Then is the account of these long nights of yours not being kept! It is being kept. You cannot see it, that is all. The day filth was placed on him in the courtyard of the Ka‘bah, he too could not see the well of Badr.
blocks.75: But it had already been written.
blocks.77: In today’s lesson we saw how, after proposals and threats had no effect, Quraysh laid hands on him. The filth placed on his back in prostration in the courtyard of the Ka‘bah. The cloak wound around his throat. The oath to put a foot on his neck, and the retreat. The thorns spread on the road. The dirt thrown into the cooking pot. And those small daily blows.
blocks.78: In so many days his hand did not once rise. He only carried on the work. And two persons are worth remembering separately. One Abu Bakr (RA); who pushed through the crowd and stepped forward. The other Fatimah (RA); in whose hand there was no power at all.
blocks.79: Both stopped it. And the rest saw and went away. And three men would come at night to listen to the Qur’an in secret. They knew the word was true. Yet they did not accept; because accepting meant giving something up.
blocks.80: The consolation that came down from the heavens did not speak of lifting the hardship. It spoke of sabr, and of returning to prostration. Because the religion that comes easily goes easily too. And what was built with thirteen years of hardship has not moved in fourteen hundred years.
blocks.81: Today’s question is from there. Around us whose hardship is there that everyone sees and yet no one stops! And when did I myself last stop! Today we heard of the persecution upon the Prophet {{1}} himself. But what came down upon those who stood behind him was harder still.
blocks.82: The next lesson is about them; those on whose bodies marks were left.
blocks.84: That day in the courtyard of the Ka‘bah there was a crowd, and laughter too. Only one girl stepped forward. Today I will ask myself one question, the one everyone is laughing at, do I join the laughter or stay silent?
blocks.85: Today I will swallow one laugh, and go and stand beside him, which from today I will not give up.

footnotes.0: Sahih Muslim, hadith no. 2797; via Abu Hurayrah (RA). The connection of the incident with verses 6–19 of Surah al-‘Alaq is mentioned in the hadith itself.
footnotes.2: Ibn Ishaq; Sirat Ibn Hisham. On the rubbing of dust on his head and the daughter’s weeping. The narration is of the Seerah books; it is not in Sahih al-Bukhari or Muslim. But the general matter of harassment on the road and throwing dust has come in sahih narrations too.
footnotes.3: Jami‘ al-Tirmidhi, hadith no. 2472; via Anas (RA). Imam al-Tirmidhi called the narration hasan sahih. ⚠ The phrase ‘thirty days and nights’ is in al-Tirmidhi’s narration; in Sunan Ibn Majah, hadith no. 151, ‘three days’ has come in the same incident (chain hasan, verification: al-Albani and ‘Ali Za’i). Here the reading of al-Tirmidhi has been taken. In Ibn Majah’s narration there is further, ‘no one has been hurt in the way of Allah as I have been hurt, and no one has been frightened in the way of Allah as I have been frightened.’
footnotes.7: Jami‘ al-Tirmidhi, hadith no. 2398; via Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas (RA). Imam al-Tirmidhi called the narration hasan sahih. It has come in Sunan Ibn Majah, hadith no. 4023 too.
footnotes.11: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith no. 5641; Sahih Muslim, hadith no. 2572; via ‘A’ishah and Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri (RA).

quiz.q: What did Abu Jahl say, swearing openly, he would do?
o: Place his foot on his neck while he was in prostration
Stop his prayer in the courtyard of the Ka‘bah
Cut relations with Banu Hashim
Spread thorns on the path to his house
quiz.e: He said, if I see Muhammad in prostration, I will put my foot on his neck, or rub his face in the ground. The people were waiting to see what he would do.

quiz.q: Drawing back, what did Abu Jahl tell the people he had seen?
o: A troop of horsemen advancing from behind the mountain
A black smoke had covered his eyes
A trench of fire, something terrifying, and wings
A stone from the wall of the Ka‘bah falling down
quiz.e: In the narration of Sahih Muslim he said, I saw between me and him a trench of fire, and something terrifying, and wings. Later the Prophet ﷺ said, had he gone a little further the angels would have torn him to pieces.

quiz.q: The connection of this incident of Abu Jahl with which surah of the Qur’an is mentioned in the hadith itself?
o: Surah al-Muzzammil, the verse of the command to patience
Surah al-‘Alaq, the verse about the one who obstructs
Surah Lahab, on Abu Lahab and his wife
Surah al-Kawthar, on the enemy being cut off
quiz.e: In verses 9–19 of Surah al-‘Alaq comes the one who obstructs a servant from prayer. The hadith itself mentions this connection.

quiz.q: What proof is given in the lesson that the safety of the Prophet ﷺ did not stand only on the strength of Banu Hashim?
o: Abu Talib had turned down Quraysh’s offer
Quraysh never dared to enter his house
Many people of Makkah inwardly accepted him
The day Abu Jahl advanced, no man stopped him
quiz.e: Quraysh did not fear war; they had even fought a forty-year tribal war. That day what stopped Abu Jahl was something else, which he himself described.

quiz.q: Speaking of the hunger of thirty days and nights, whose name did the Prophet ﷺ take?
o: Abu Bakr (RA), as a companion
Bilal (RA), who was with him
‘Ali (RA), a small member of the household
Khabbab (RA), one of the tortured
quiz.e: He said, for thirty days there was for me and Bilal no food that any living creature could eat; only so little as could be hidden under Bilal’s armpit.

quiz.q: When he returned home with dust rubbed on his head, who washed his head?
o: Khadijah (RA), as wife
Umm Ayman (RA), the one who raised him
His daughter Fatimah (RA)
Zaynab (RA), the eldest daughter
quiz.e: The girl came running, brought water and wept while washing his head. He said, daughter, do not weep; Allah will protect your father.

quiz.q: With the consolation in verses 97–99 of Surah al-Hijr, what was he told to do?
o: To give the enemies a counter-reply
To leave Makkah and go to another city
To keep quiet and stop the da‘wah
To glorify and return to prostration
quiz.e: To that very prostration where he had been humiliated he was told to return. Because from the place where the blow lands, the strength comes from there too.

quiz.q: What meaning of ‘sabr’ is drawn in the lesson from the verses of consolation?
o: Silently enduring everything
Cutting all relations with the enemy
Putting revenge aside for later
Carrying on the work without stopping it
quiz.e: Nowhere in the verses is it said that the hardship will be lifted; it is said that help will come. Even with filth on him he stood again the next day in the courtyard of the Ka‘bah; that is sabr.

quiz.q: According to the narration of al-Tirmidhi, on whom does the most severe test come among people?
o: The prophets; then those nearest to them
The poor; then helpless women and children
The rulers; then their followers
The scholars; then ordinary Muslims
quiz.e: The rule is stated in the hadith too; a person is tested according to his religion. The stronger one is in religion, the harder his test.

quiz.q: How is the meaning of ‘a person is tested according to his religion’ explained in the lesson?
o: Hardship is not proof of Allah’s displeasure, rather the opposite
Hardship itself is proof of a high rank for a person
The more one sins, the more his hardship
The hardship of the world is the advance form of the punishment of the Hereafter
quiz.e: We think hardship means Allah has turned away; the hadith says exactly the opposite. But hardship in itself is no rank; the rank lies in standing firm within the hardship.

quiz.q: Who said the words ‘when will Allah’s help come’ in verse 214 of Surah al-Baqarah?
o: Ordinary people of earlier nations
The persecuted weak Muslims of Makkah
The Messenger and the believers with him
Those who went back after believing
quiz.e: That means asking this question is not a sin; the sin is asking the question and stopping. And the last word of the verse is, Allah’s help is near.

quiz.q: If Allah willed He could have stopped everything in a moment; why did He not?
o: Because the time for Quraysh to believe had not come
Because the test is itself a part of the system
Because the angels had not yet been sent down
Because the people of Makkah were not deserving of punishment
quiz.e: In verse 2 of Surah al-‘Ankabut it is said, do people think that they will be left alone because they say, we have believed, and not be tested!

quiz.q: To a person who has made supplication for years and nothing is changing, which word does the lesson recall?
o: The words of the supplication must be changed and said anew
Charity must be given before each supplication
Not being accepted and being accepted late are not the same
Reduce supplication and turn the mind to deeds
quiz.e: Allah’s clock does not match our clock. The thirteen years of Makkah are proof; Allah did not stop it each day, each day He sent consolation.

quiz.q: From the hadith ‘even if a thorn pricks, Allah erases sins in exchange’, what did the lesson mean to convey?
o: One should not be restless over minor hardships
The account of every hardship is being kept
When hardship comes treatment may be skipped
Hardship always means punishment for sin
quiz.e: If the account of even one thorn is kept, then is the account of your long nights not being kept! It is being kept; you simply cannot see it.
